one_liner: HubSpot has a broad REST API with self-serve OAuth2 apps, free developer accounts, service keys/private tokens, and an official remote MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for public apps (multi-account distribution requires OAuth). Static tokens: service keys, private/static app access tokens (Bearer) for single-account use.
access_notes: Free developer account with test accounts and API access; free CRM plan includes API access. Installing apps requires Super Admin in the target account.
blocker_notes: No blocker; free developer account and test accounts allow building and testing.

evidence.quote: HubSpot supports the [OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code grant type]
There are two ways to authenticate calls to HubSpot’s APIs:
you can use service keys to query HubSpot’s [REST APIs](/docs/api-reference/latest/overview) directly without having to use the CLI
You can create a free HubSpot account and build apps without a paid subscription.
**API access** to HubSpot’s public APIs for development and testing
The API is a set of web addresses at api.hubapi.com, one family per object, with the data as JSON.
You can create up to 1,000 [webhook subscriptions](/docs/api-reference/latest/webhooks) per app.
The remote HubSpot MCP server is a publicly hosted endpoint for connecting external AI tools and applications to HubSpot’s CRM.
configuring your MCP client to connect to the HubSpot MCP server at `https://mcp.hubspot.com` using your connector’s OAuth credentials.
